title: Solari
description: Your household finances in Solari: spending, budgets, cash flow, goals and net worth.

tools.name: UpdateAccountBalanceHistory
tools.description:
Write balance history to a manual account, replacing the dates the entries cover. What is replaced cannot be recovered. Find the account id with GetAccounts. GetNetWorthHistory with account_ids, interval "day" and include_account_breakdown shows the existing balances, but converted to the household base currency and only for accounts that count in net worth: for an account in another currency, do not write those figures back as they are.

Only manual accounts can be written: an account connected to a bank or valued from its holdings is rejected. Every day from the first to the last entry is rewritten, and a day without an entry takes the previous entry's balance. After the last entry, its balance carries forward up to the next saved day, or up to today when there is none, and then it becomes the account's current balance. Days outside that range do not change. It is all or nothing, and no transaction is created.

Balances are in the account currency and signed as GetAccounts reports them: on a liability, what is owed is positive. Solari stores them with the decimals of the currency. Dates can go back 30 years, not past today in the household, and span at most 4000 days.

With dry_run true nothing is written and the answer is the same one the write would give: the date range, snapshots_to_write, existing_snapshots_in_range_to_replace, would_update_current_balance and the current balance before and after.

tools.name: UpdateAccountDebtDetails
tools.description:
Update the debt details stored on a liability account and return them. Pass only the fields to change; null removes a value.

Rates are percentages: 6.99 means 6.99%, with at most three decimals. Solari keeps one rate per account, so apr and interest_rate are the same value and only one can be passed. Payments are in the account currency; the planned payment may be below the minimum payment, and a planned payment of 0 means no plan (the minimum is used). The values are saved on the account and apply everywhere in Solari, including GetDebtPaydownPlan.

tools.name: CreateGoal
tools.description:
Create a savings goal for the household and return it.

Every goal in Solari has a target amount, in the household base currency, and a target date needs it. A new goal starts with a zero balance: use AllocateToGoal to set aside part of an account balance for it, or UpdateGoal with account_ids_to_link to dedicate a whole account to it. A target date is stored as the last day of its month. The type is what the goal is for; it does not change any amount, it is kept when the goal is renamed, and it cannot be changed later.

tools.name: UpdateGoal
tools.description:
Edit a savings goal and/or change which accounts are linked to it, and return it. Pass only what changes; what is not passed stays as it is.

The target is in the household base currency. A target date is stored as the last day of its month, and null removes it; a goal without a target amount takes a date only together with one.

Linking dedicates the whole account to the goal: the goal follows what is free in the account (its balance minus what other goals hold there), and the account takes no other allocation until it is unlinked. An account can be linked only if it takes part in goals (the person chooses which ones in Solari) and is not a debt. Other goals keep their allocations in it, but if the account is linked to another goal, it moves to this one and that goal drops to zero from it. An allocation this goal already has stays in its history, and an adjustment covers the rest. Linking and unlinking are recorded as adjustments and do not count in the budget. Linking an account that is already linked changes nothing. Only linked accounts can be unlinked; for a partial allocation use ReduceGoalAllocation.

Everything is checked before anything is written. The changes are then applied one by one, so if a call fails midway it is safe to repeat it.

tools.name: AllocateToGoal
tools.description:
Set aside part of an account's balance for a savings goal. No money moves: the account balance stays the same and less of it is available.

The amount is positive and in the account currency; Solari converts it to the base currency with the rate of the movement date. It is never capped: an amount above what is available in the account is rejected with goals.error.excede_disponible and nothing is written. The account must take part in goals (the person chooses which ones in Solari), cannot be a debt and cannot be linked to a goal (goals.error.cuenta_dedicada). An archived goal takes no allocations (goals.error.objetivo_archivado). Calling it again adds to the allocation. The movement counts in the budget actuals of its month. Returns the goal, allocated_amount and account_available, what is left in the account.

tools.name: GetAccounts
tools.description:
List the household's accounts with their current balances.

An account the household wrote notes on carries them in notes; accounts without notes have no notes field. Each balance comes in the account currency and in the household base currency. Liabilities (kind "liability") hold what is owed as a positive number, and carry debt: interest_rate (annual percentage, the APR of a credit card), minimum_payment, planned_payment and credit_limit in the account currency (null when not set), and exclude_from_debt_paydown; UpdateAccountDebtDetails changes them. Also returns total assets, total liabilities and net worth in the base currency; these always count every account that belongs to net worth, including hidden ones and regardless of the filters. All filters intersect. owner_user_id is the household member who owns the account, or null for a joint account; business_id is its business, if any. ownership narrows the list to one person: with scope "user" you get that person's accounts and the joint ones, or only theirs with jointly_owned_setting false. Pass an account id to the tools that take account_id or account_ids, such as GetTransactions, GetNetWorthHistory, GetCashFlow, GetInvestments, CreateTransaction, CreateTransfer, UpdateAccountBalanceHistory, UpdateAccountDebtDetails, AllocateToGoal and CreateRule. Read filters also take names (the *_names fields) next to ids; resolved_names in the response says what each name matched.

tools.name: CreateAccount
tools.description:
Create a manual account in the household and return it as GetAccounts lists it.

Manual means Solari does not sync it with a bank: its balance moves with the transactions written to it (CreateTransaction, CreateTransfer) and with UpdateAccountBalanceHistory. Assets are cash_bank, investment, real_estate, vehicles, valuables and other_assets; liabilities are credit_cards, mortgage, loans and other_liabilities. A cryptocurrency wallet is an investment account.

initial_balance is the balance on initial_balance_date (today if left out), in the account currency: for a liability, what is owed, as a positive number. It is saved as a balance adjustment on that day, as the app does. An investment account follows its total balance by default; with tracking "holdings" its value comes from its holdings instead, which are added in the app, so it starts empty and takes no initial_balance. Before creating, check with GetAccounts that the account does not exist yet: calling this twice creates two accounts. If reading it back fails after it is created, the error carries created_account_id: the account already exists, so do not create it again.

tools.name: GetNetWorthHistory
tools.description:
Get the household's net worth over time, in its base currency, as dated readings of net worth, total assets and total liabilities.

By default readings are daily for ranges up to 31 days, weekly up to 92 days and monthly beyond that. Each reading is the balance at the end of its day, week (Monday to Sunday) or month, or at end_date if that comes first; balances are never added up over time. Other currencies are converted at the rate of each reading's date. Liabilities are what is owed, as a positive number. Accounts excluded from net worth never count; hidden ones do. All filters intersect; a filter that matches no account returns no readings. ownership narrows to one person: with scope "user" you get that person's accounts and the joint ones, or only theirs with jointly_owned_setting false. earliest_data_date is the first day with a balance in the accounts that match the filters, whatever the date range, or null if there is none.

Limits: 366 days for daily readings, 728 days for weekly, 360 months for monthly, and, with include_account_breakdown, 25 accounts and 3000 balances in total, readings times accounts (narrow it with account_ids, account_types or account_sub_types).

tools.name: GetTransactions
tools.description:
Search the household's transactions, most recent first, or read some of them by id.

Each transaction has its id, date, type, description (the notes the person wrote, null if none), merchant, category and account with their ids, tags, needs_review and pending; pass the id to UpdateTransaction, BulkUpdateTransactions or DeleteTransaction. UpdateTransactionSplits takes the id of a transaction that is not split, or the split total's id, which for a part is split_parent_id (returned with include_details). The bank's own text is original_description, returned with include_details together with cleansed_description, the same text without card numbers, IBANs, references, dates and times (null when nothing is left).

Amounts are signed from the point of view of the account: money going out is negative. Each one comes in the account currency and in the household base currency, converted at the rate of its day. Split transactions appear as their parts, never as the parent, and each part is matched by its own category, merchant and tags. Hidden transactions are left out unless visibility says otherwise. A pending transaction is one the bank has not posted yet: its amount and date may still change and it may disappear, it never counts in the account balance, and it counts in budgets, cash flow and reports only if the household allows editing pending transactions. All filters intersect; the exclude_ filters keep what has no value for that field. Results are paged: when has_more is true, call again with offset set to next_offset. With transaction_ids, not_found_ids lists what does not exist, was deleted or belongs to another household. deleted_transaction_visibility reads what a person or an assistant deleted, only since Solari records it. Read filters also take names (the *_names fields) next to ids; resolved_names in the response says what each name matched.

tools.name: CreateTransaction
tools.description:
Create a manual expense or income in an account of the household and return it.

The sign of amount decides the type, with the same convention as GetTransactions: negative is an expense, positive is income. It is in the account currency and cannot have more decimals than that currency allows. The account balance moves with it. Household rules run on the new transaction, so the returned category, tags or split may differ from what was sent. To record money that went between two accounts of the household, use CreateTransfer: an expense in one account plus income in the other would count as spending and income in budgets and reports. All references are ids from the read tools.

If hiding it or reading it back fails after it is created, the error carries created_transaction_id: the transaction already exists, so do not create it again.

tools.name: CreateTransfer
tools.description:
Record a transfer between two accounts of the household and return both sides of it. It only writes the record in Solari: it never moves money at a bank.

Use this, never CreateTransaction, to record money that went from one account of the household to another (paying a credit card from a checking account, saving into a savings account, a cash withdrawal). It creates one transfer with two linked transactions: a transfer_out in the source account and a transfer_in in the destination. Both balances move, and a transfer never counts as spending or income in budgets and reports, while an expense plus an income would inflate both.

amount is what leaves the source account, positive and in its currency. When both accounts share a currency, the same amount arrives and destination_amount must be left out or be equal. When the currencies differ, destination_amount is required: what arrives, in the destination currency. Amounts cannot have more decimals than their currency allows. Holdings are not moved: to move shares or funds between investment accounts, use the app. All references are ids from GetAccounts.

tools.name: GetCashFlow
tools.description:
Run a flexible cash flow query over a date range, in two stages. All amounts are in the household base currency, converted at the rate of each day.

Stage 1 (base_query) buckets income and expense by time, by an entity, or both. Transfers never count in income, expense or net. A split counts by its parts. A refund reduces the expense of its category. Each row has income, expense (positive spending) and amount (income minus expense). Money with no category, merchant or business comes in a row with entity_id null, so rows always add up to the totals. When grouping by account, a hidden account has its own row like any other; an account whose transactions are hidden adds nothing. With needs_review_by_user, entity_id is the user_id of the person who has to review and entity_name their name; everything else, including what is waiting for no one in particular, is in the entity_id null row. A time-only query lists every bucket, including empty ones; with an entity, only buckets with money are listed.

Transfers, only when asked: with category_type transfer you get just the money moved between household accounts, as a side apart that never adds to income, expense or net (those read zero). Each transfer has two legs: transfers_out is the leg that left an account and transfers_in the leg that arrived, each in the base currency at the rate of its own day and in its own account, so grouping by account shows where money left and where it arrived. transfers_net is transfers_in minus transfers_out, also in the base currency: per account, what the account gained (positive) or lost (negative) through transfers; over the whole household it is near zero, and only the exchange rates of each leg's day, or a leg outside the filters, move it. Never add transfers_out and transfers_in together: that counts each transfer twice. All filters work on each leg; category_ids only accepts transfer categories. In post_aggregation, use measure transfers_out or transfers_in.

Filters intersect. Read filters also take names (the *_names fields) next to ids; resolved_names in the response says what each name matched. The exclude_ filters keep what has no value for that field: excluding a category keeps uncategorized money. Parts of a split are matched one by one, with their own category, merchant and tags. ownership_setting works on the owner of each transaction: with scope "user" you get that person's transactions and the joint ones, or only theirs with jointly_owned_setting false.

Stage 2 (post_aggregation, optional) reduces those buckets over the complete grid: every period of the range crossed with every entity that appears, empty ones at zero. So avg divides by all buckets including the zero ones: 180 over three months is 60 even if one month had nothing. sum and avg give one row per group, count gives how many buckets have a non-zero measure (value is a plain number), and max and min give the top or bottom N buckets per group.

Limits: 400 time buckets, 36 periods with money when also grouping by category, group, merchant or business, 50 accounts when grouping by account, and 500 rows per page (use offset and next_offset). A query Solari cannot answer exactly returns invalid_input with the reason, never an approximate figure.

tools.description:
Project the household's debt payoff plan without saving anything.

Avalanche pays the highest-rate debt first and rolls freed payments to the next debt. Snowball pays the smallest balance first and rolls freed payments to the next debt. Planned follows each debt's own payment without rollover; extra payments, if any, go to the debts in list order (oldest account first). Extra monthly or one-time payments are hypothetical and are never saved.

The projection starts in the household's current month and every total is in the household base currency. Top-level projected_interest, projected_total and debt_free_date are for the selected method including extras, and match the account rows. baseline is every debt paid at its own current payment with no rollover and no extras: compare against it to answer "how much sooner" or "how much interest saved"; savings already holds that comparison (null for planned). If any projected debt is not paid off within 100 years, projected_interest, projected_total and debt_free_date are null, debt_free_beyond_100_years is true and notes says so; that debt's own row has null too. A debt whose payment does not cover its interest is still projected, and the other debts' freed payments pay it off.

Debts left out of the projection are in accounts_not_projected with a reason: excluded_from_paydown, missing_details (see missing: a rate, or a payment) or no_balance. Hidden accounts are included like any other. Each account row has rate_field, the UpdateAccountDebtDetails field that holds its rate ('apr' for credit cards, 'interest_rate' otherwise), and yearly_balances: the projected balance in the base currency at the start, on each January 1 and on the payoff date (empty when there is no payoff date). Each list returns at most 100 rows; accounts_total and accounts_not_projected_total say how many exist, and the totals always count every projected debt.

List the merchants of the household, most used first: the ones its members created and the ones from Solari's catalog (such as big supermarket chains) that its transactions use.

Each merchant comes with its merchant_id, the name people see in Solari and how many transactions use it; split transactions count as their parts. Merchants without transactions are left out unless you ask for them, and catalog merchants the household has never used are never listed. total counts every merchant that matches, across all pages. Results are paged, up to 200 per page: when has_more is true, call again with offset set to next_offset. Pass merchant_id to the tools that take merchant ids.

tools.name: ListRules
tools.description:
List the household's transaction rules in the order they run, including the ones created by other household members.

Each rule has its criteria (a transaction must meet all of them) and its actions. Every reference to a category, account, tag, merchant, goal or business comes as { id, name }, and every person as { user_id, name }. name is null when the item no longer exists or has no name; in the owner and business criteria, a null id means shared and personal respectively. An action set to null clears that field, and an action that is absent leaves it alone. Rule amounts have no currency of their own: they are compared with each transaction's amount in its account currency. Results are paged, up to 500 per page: when has_more is true, call again with offset set to next_offset.

Criteria: merchant_names, category_ids, account_ids, amount_min, amount_max. Amounts are positive and is_expense is required with them: true for expenses, false for income. tools.name: GetBudget
tools.description:
Get the household's budget for a range of months, up to 24. Dates are moved to the first day of their month.

Lines are per category, plus one per group budgeted as a whole or one for the flexible bucket, depending on budget_system. counts_in_totals says whether a line adds to the totals: use the totals rather than adding lines up, because a group or bucket budget replaces its categories. The goal_contributions list has the planned goal payments and debt_contributions the planned debt payments. totals_by_month and totals_overall give the budgeted income and expenses, the planned contributions (their goal_contributions already includes the debt payments, so do not add debt_contributions to it) and what is left unallocated, plus the actuals with include_actuals. totals_by_group gives each group's planned amount and, with include_actuals, its actual, difference and status. A budget that does not exist is null, never 0, and lines with nothing to show are left out. With include_actuals, each line also has what was spent or earned, the rollover from previous months, difference (what is left, rollover included) and a status: over_budget, under_budget or on_budget. All amounts are in the household base currency, and split transactions count through their parts. Returns at most 1000 lines per list: when truncated is true, ask for fewer months; the totals always cover the whole range.

tools.name: GetRecurring
tools.description:
List the household's active recurring plans: paychecks, bills, subscriptions and transfers.

Returns four buckets: income, expenses, credit card payments and transfers. Credit card payments and transfers only move money between accounts and are never part of the expense bucket. Each item has its id, name, amount in the account currency and in the household base currency, frequency (every interval_count days, weeks, months or years), next date, last paid date (null if never paid; a skipped occurrence is not a payment), category and account. Each bucket's total adds one occurrence of every item in the base currency; an item whose amount_in_base is null (in another currency and without a converted amount, as when it has no next date) is not in it. It is not a monthly figure. Returns at most 200 items per bucket: when truncated is true, item_count and total still cover them all.

With include_pending, suspected recurring items are added too: merchants whose last charges repeat with a steady rhythm and amount but that have no plan yet and are waiting for the household to review them. They are mixed into the income and expense buckets and count in item_count and total. Then every item carries a status: "active" for a plan, "suspected" for a suspected item. A suspected item is not a plan yet: its id is null and suggestion_id identifies the suggestion. Its amount is the latest charge, converted at that charge's date; last_paid_date is the latest charge, next_date is the next expected charge (one or more periods after it, never in the past), occurrences is how many charges support it and recent_dates are the latest of them.
